full_text_en:
Xiamen Powder Metallurgy Factory v. Xiamen Kaiyuan District Hengzhu Metal Products Factory, Chen Kunxi, and Chen Mengzong — appeal of dispute over trade secret infringement

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Fujian Province Xiamen Powder Metallurgy Products Factory.
Legal Representative: Liu Yiji, Factory Director.

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Fujian Province Xiamen Kaiyuan District Hengzhu Metal Products Factory.
Legal Representative: Chen Liming, Factory Director.

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Chen Mengzong, male, 42 years old, residing at the dormitory of Xiamen Powder Metallurgy Factory, Fujian Province.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Chen Kunxi, male, 40 years old, residing at Hongtang Village, Tong'an County, Fujian Province.

The appellants, Xiamen Powder Metallurgy Factory, Xiamen Kaiyuan District Hengzhu Metal Products Factory, and Chen Mengzong, dissatisfied with the civil judgment of the Xiamen Intermediate People's Court in the case of dispute over trade secret infringement, appealed to the Fujian High People's Court.

After ascertaining the facts at first instance, the Xiamen Intermediate People's Court found that the technologies used by Xiamen Powder Metallurgy Factory (hereinafter referred to as the Powder Factory) in the sintering technology of bronze porous elements, including die design, die loading, die unloading, temperature control during sintering, production of threaded products, and sintering of products with different particle sizes, were proprietary technologies introduced by the Powder Factory. These proprietary technologies constituted the commercial advantage of the Powder Factory in operating its bronze porous element products and were trade secrets of the Powder Factory. Chen Kunxi and Chen Mengzong, without authorization, used these trade secrets in Xiamen Kaiyuan District Hengzhu Metal Products Factory (hereinafter referred to as Hengzhu Factory), which they had jointly invested in, thereby constituting infringement. Hengzhu Factory, as the entity that implemented the technology, was to bear joint and several liability. Accordingly, on December 23, 1993, the court rendered the following judgment: (1) Hengzhu Factory shall cease using the technologies identical to those of the Powder Factory, including die design, die loading, die unloading, temperature control during sintering, unified sintering of different particle sizes, and manufacture of threaded products; (2) Chen Kunxi and Chen Mengzong shall each compensate the Powder Factory for economic losses in the amount of RMB 13,200.50, and Hengzhu Factory shall bear joint and several liability for the above compensation. After the judgment, the Powder Factory appealed, arguing that the first-instance judgment found the defendants had infringed for over four years but only ordered compensation of over RMB 20,000, which was far from the actual losses, and requested compensation of RMB 450,000. Hengzhu Factory and Chen Mengzong appealed, arguing that the Powder Factory had not taken confidentiality measures for the technology, such as selling used dies to a scrap company and providing die drawings to other factories for processing dies, which had made the technology public; therefore, there was no infringement of trade secrets, and requested that the Powder Factory's claims be dismissed. Chen Kunxi also replied on the same grounds.

The Fujian High People's Court, upon trial, found the following facts:

On June 15, 1984, Xiamen Instrument and Meter Company entered into a "Technology Transfer Contract for the Manufacture of Sintered Bronze Porous Elements" with a foreign company, stipulating that the foreign company would transfer to the Powder Factory, through Xiamen Instrument and Meter Company, the proprietary technology and related drawings and technical materials for manufacturing bronze porous elements. The contract was valid for eight years. During the contract period and for five years after its expiration, the transferee had no right to transfer any information within the scope of the contract to any third party outside the contract. This project was one of the technology introduction projects approved by the former Ministry of Machinery Industry in 1983 under Document No. (83) Ji Ji Han Zi 1489. After the contract was signed, the Powder Factory sent technical personnel, including the appellee Chen Kunxi, abroad for training. The content of the training was confirmed in writing by both the transferor and the transferee, and it was recorded that Chen Kunxi studied the design of product dies and related process technology. Thereafter, the Powder Factory organized the trained technical personnel to digest and absorb the introduced technology, and the achievements won the Third Prize for Scientific and Technological Achievements of Xiamen City. At that time, both Chen Kunxi and Chen Mengzong were engaged in technical or management work in the workshop producing bronze porous elements. Chen Kunxi had signed a professional technical personnel employment contract with the Powder Factory, which included a clause stipulating that during the employment period, he "shall not use his position or work convenience to seek personal gain or infringe upon the enterprise's technical rights and economic interests." In August 1988, Chen Kunxi, Chen Mengzong, and Xiamen Kaiyuan District Hengzhu Production Service Community jointly invested in and established the Hengzhu Factory, with a registered capital of RMB 100,000. Chen Kunxi and Chen Mengzong contributed RMB 41,379 and RMB 23,901, respectively. In June 1990, Hengzhu Factory selected, processed, and repaired used dies sold by the Powder Factory from a scrap recycling company, then used them to produce bronze porous elements identical to those of the Powder Factory and placed them on the market, resulting in a decline in the sales volume of the Powder Factory's products. Consequently, a dispute arose between the parties. During the first instance, investigations were conducted with the China Powder Metallurgy Association, Beijing No. 2 Powder Metallurgy Factory, Beijing Powder Metallurgy Research Institute, and Liao Jichang, the Director of the Powder Metallurgy Research Office of Northwest Nonferrous Metals Research Institute and a powder metallurgy expert. These units and experts all opined that the technology held by the Powder Factory was unique and advanced nationwide. The first-instance court also commissioned an expert appraisal group to compare the technology used by Hengzhu Factory with that of the Powder Factory. The similarities found were: (1) the structure and material of the dies, the loose powder loading method, the die unloading method, die unloading tools, and shaping method were the same; (2) the continuous operation principles of furnace entry, preheating, sintering, holding, cooling, and furnace exit during the sintering process were the same, but specific operating parameters differed. At second instance, it was ascertained that the sales revenue of Hengzhu Factory's bronze porous element products was RMB 1,145,912.53. Based on the metal metallurgy industry association's certification that the industry's gross profit margin is generally 15.57% of sales revenue, the gross profit obtained by Hengzhu Factory from the sale of these products was calculated to be RMB 178,418.50.

The above facts are confirmed by the contract between Xiamen Instrument and Meter Company and the foreign company, the confirmation drawings provided by the foreign company to the Powder Factory, testimony from relevant departments and experts, the written expert appraisal conclusion commissioned by the first-instance court, relevant business documents of Hengzhu Factory, and the employment contract signed between Chen Kunxi and the Powder Factory.

The Fujian High People's Court held that: The bronze porous element sintering proprietary technology acquired by the appellant Powder Factory through technology transfer, after digestion and absorption, had given the Powder Factory a competitive advantage in the same industry nationwide. To prevent the technology from becoming known to the public, the Powder Factory limited access to a few relevant personnel and took appropriate confidentiality measures. This technology had become a trade secret of the Powder Factory and, in accordance with Article 5 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, was protected by law. The Powder Factory, as the lawful holder of the trade secret, was the rights holder of that trade secret. Chen Kunxi and Chen Mengzong, as employees of the Powder Factory who possessed and understood the trade secret, had a legal obligation under Article 6 of the General Principles of the Civil Law to maintain the confidentiality of the enterprise's trade secrets. However, they knowingly disclosed and used the trade secret in the Hengzhu Factory, in which they jointly invested with others, enabling that factory to produce and sell products identical to those of the Powder Factory, thereby causing economic losses to the Powder Factory. In accordance with Article 10, item (2) of the Law of the People's Republic of China Against Unfair Competition, the actions of Chen Kunxi, Chen Mengzong, and Hengzhu Factory constituted the use of the rights holder's trade secrets obtained by improper means. Pursuant to Article 20, paragraph 1 of the Law Against Unfair Competition, Chen Kunxi, Chen Mengzong, and Hengzhu Factory shall jointly bear liability for damages arising from the infringement. As for the defense of Chen Kunxi and the arguments of Chen Mengzong and Hengzhu Factory on appeal that the Powder Factory's actions of entrusting the processing of dies for the bronze porous element sintering proprietary technology to other factories and selling used dies to a scrap company had made the technology public, since it was difficult for uninformed persons to know how to use the dies, it was impossible for them to select used dies from the scrap company, repair them, and use them. Therefore, the grounds for the appeal and defense are untenable. The first-instance judgment's order that Hengzhu Factory cease using the Powder Factory's proprietary technology and that Chen Kunxi and Chen Mengzong bear compensation liability was correct, but the amount of compensation was too low, and the judgment did not determine the compensation liability of Hengzhu Factory, which should be corrected. In accordance with Article 153, paragraph 1, item (3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the court rendered the following judgment on September 19, 1994:

1. Affirm item (1) of the Civil Judgment (1990) Xia Zhong Fa Jing Min Zi No. 28 of the Xiamen Intermediate People's Court;
2. Reverse item (2) of the Civil Judgment (1990) Xia Zhong Fa Jing Min Zi No. 28 of the Xiamen Intermediate People's Court;
3. Chen Kunxi, Chen Mengzong, and Xiamen Kaiyuan District Hengzhu Metal Products Factory shall, within 30 days from the effective date of this judgment, compensate Xiamen Powder Metallurgy Products Factory for economic losses in the amount of RMB 178,418.50. Chen Kunxi and Chen Mengzong shall each bear 40% thereof, and Hengzhu Factory shall bear 20% thereof. The above compensation liability shall be joint and several.

Court acceptance fee for this case: RMB 9,260. Xiamen Powder Metallurgy Products Factory to bear RMB 4,000; Chen Kunxi to bear RMB 2,000; Chen Mengzong to bear RMB 2,000; Xiamen Kaiyuan District Hengzhu Metal Products Factory to bear RMB 1,260. The litigation fees borne by Chen Kunxi, Chen Mengzong, and Hengzhu Factory shall be subject to joint and several liability.
